title: Deputy Director, Partnerships & Technical Integration
description:
Job Title: Deputy Director, Partnerships & Technical Integration

Job Location: Milpitas, CA or Remote (US)

Salary: $196,000-$210,000

Department: Workforce Development, NNME


Although we’re small, we’re mighty and influence and impact society at large positively. At SEMI, we offer opportunities to connect and interact with world leaders, industry legends, and rising stars. We help our members develop public and private policies to strengthen global supply chains and promote business growth and prosperity. Learn and grow professionally through career opportunities such as rotational assignments. Contribute by influencing and impacting an industry that is the foundation for innovation and positive change in areas like environmental sustainability, thought leadership, and workforce development. We take pride in offering work-life balance so you can live your personal and professional life to the fullest.


As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome all to apply

SEMI Foundation | National Network for Microelectronics Education (NNME)


The Opportunity:

The U.S. is projected to significantly fall short semiconductor workers by 2030 against more than $390 billion in announced investment. NNME exists to close that gap.


Backed by the U.S. National Science Foundation in partnership with the Department of Commerce, NNME currently connects four Regional Nodes and more than 325 performer organizations into a single national system. The SEMI Foundation serves as National Coordinating Hub, drawing on a global association of over 4,000 microelectronics companies.


This role is for a semiconductor leader who wants their technical judgment to shape how an entire country trains its workforce, at national scale, with federal backing, at the moment it matters most.


Position Summary

The National Network for Microelectronics Education (NNME) seeks a senior semiconductor industry leader to serve as Deputy Director, Partnerships & Technical Integration. In partnership with the Director for Education, Evaluation & Network Performance, this executive will ensure NNME's workforce, education, and partnership strategies remain technically relevant, industry-informed, and responsive to current and emerging needs of the U.S. semiconductor ecosystem.

As the primary technical and industry liaison between NNME and the broader semiconductor ecosystem, this leader will leverage the unique position of the SEMI Foundation to connect NNME and its Regional Nodes with employers, technical experts, emerging technologies, workforce intelligence, and strategic partnerships.

The role provides leadership at the intersection of semiconductor technology, workforce development, industry engagement, artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, and national workforce strategy.


Key Responsibilities

Industry & Technology Alignment

  • Lead NNME's strategy to align semiconductor technology and industry needs with workforce development and educational outcomes.
  • Monitor technology trends and assess implications for occupations, workforce demand, skills, and education pathways.
  • Ensure workforce and education initiatives reflect current industry practices, tools, technologies, and standards.
  • Translate industry intelligence into actionable recommendations for NNME leadership and Regional Nodes, so initiatives reflect current practices and standards.

Technical Quality, Validation & Workforce Intelligence

  • Ensure technical quality and industry relevance across NNME workforce and education initiatives.
  • Ensure strong industry validation processes for pathways, curricula, credentials, and competency frameworks, engaging employers, technical experts, and industry advisors to validate workforce requirements and educational strategies.
  • Liaise with the NNME Technical Consultant Working Group
  • Lead workforce intelligence efforts, identifying emerging occupations, skills, technologies, and future workforce needs and connecting those demand signals to training, credentialing, and pathway development strategies.

AI, Automation & Emerging Technologies

  • Lead NNME's strategy related to artificial intelligence, automation, smart manufacturing, and other emerging technologies.
  • Assess the impact of technological change on semiconductor occupations and workforce requirements.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage AI-enabled tools, simulations, workforce intelligence, learning technologies, and digital solutions to strengthen workforce development outcomes.
  • Ensure NNME strategies remain aligned with evolving industry technology priorities.

Strategic Partnerships & SEMI Engagement

  • Serve as NNME's primary industry and technical liaison to SEMI Americas.
  • Build and maintain relationships with semiconductor employers, SEMI member companies, technical communities, and national partners.
  • Leverage SEMI's ecosystem to provide expertise, market intelligence, standards knowledge, and workforce insights to NNME and Regional Nodes.
  • Represent NNME in industry, workforce, government, research, and education forums.
  • Strengthen employer participation in workforce planning, validation activities, experiential learning, and talent development initiatives.

Regional Node & National Ecosystem Support

  • Identify strategic technical support for NNME Regional Nodes.
  • Facilitate access to technical experts, employer partners, and industry resources.
  • Support national Communities of Practice focused on technology, industry alignment, and emerging technologies.
  • Support collaboration among employers, educators, workforce organizations, researchers, and government partners.
  • Contribute to NNME strategic planning, sustainability initiatives, and long-term workforce ecosystem development.

Executive Leadership

  • Serve as a visionary and inspiring leader within the NNME and contribute to overall organizational strategy, management, and health.
  • Collaborate with SEMI Foundation leadership, federal partners, industry stakeholders, and Regional Nodes to ensure NNME success.
  • Provide industry perspective to the NNME on performance assessment, continuous improvement, and strategic priorities.
  • Help ensure NNME remains responsive to workforce needs while anticipating future industry requirements.

Qualifications

Required

  • Minimum 12 years of progressively responsible experience in the semiconductor or microelectronics industry.
  • Demonstrated extensive senior leadership experience in semiconductor technology, manufacturing, workforce development, operations, engineering, or related functions.
  • Deep knowledge of the semiconductor ecosystem, including manufacturing, equipment, materials, packaging, testing, workforce requirements, and industry trends.
  • Experience translating technical and industry requirements into workforce, education, training, competency, or credentialing strategies.
  • Knowledge of competency frameworks, occupational standards, curriculum alignment, and industry validation practices.
  • Understanding of emerging technologies including AI, automation, advanced manufacturing, digital transformation, and related trends.
  • Proven success building strategic partnerships across industry, government, workforce, education, and research sectors.
  • Exceptional written and oral communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Exceptional management and leadership skills; adept at engaging, supporting, and leading highly skilled teams.

Preferred

  • Advanced degree in engineering, materials science, physics, business, workforce development, or related discipline.
  • Experience with SEMI, industry associations, or technology consortia.
  • Experience in semiconductor workforce development, education, training, career pathways, or credentialing initiatives.
  • Familiarity with CHIPS-related initiatives, NSF-funded programs, Microelectronics Commons, or similar national investments.
  • Experience with workforce forecasting, technology roadmapping, smart manufacturing, AI applications, or industry standards development.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means NNME workforce and education strategies consistently reflect current and future semiconductor workforce needs. The Deputy Director will establish strong industry partnerships, ensure educational pathways and credentials remain employer-validated, leverage SEMI's industry ecosystem as a strategic advantage, and position NNME to anticipate technological change rather than react to it. The result will be a stronger, nationally connected semiconductor workforce ecosystem that supports long-term U.S. competitiveness and workforce development goals.


About NNME

The National Network for Microelectronics Education (NNME) is a national workforce development initiative supported by the U.S. National Science Foundation in partnership with the U.S. Department of Commerce. The SEMI Foundation serves as the NNME Coordinating Hub, connecting industry, education, workforce systems, and regional partners to strengthen America's semiconductor and microelectronics workforce pipeline.


The SEMI Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit charitable organization founded in 2001 to support economic opportunity for workers and the sustained growth of the microelectronics industry. We accomplish this through creating pathways and opportunities for job seekers, and tools and systems for semiconductor companies to attract, develop, and retain a diverse, innovative, and skilled workforce. Visit us at semifoundation.org. SEMI is our parent company.


ABOUT SEMI

SEMI® is the global industry association connecting over 4,000 companies and 1.5 million professionals worldwide across the semiconductor and electronics design and manufacturing supply chain. We accelerate member collaboration on solutions to top industry challenges through Advocacy, Workforce Development, Sustainability, Supply Chain Management and other programs. Our SEMICON® expositions and events, technology coalitions, standards and market intelligence help advance our members’ business growth and innovations in design, devices, equipment, materials, services and software, enabling smarter, faster, more secure electronics. Visit , contact a regional office, and connect with SEMI on LinkedIn and X to learn more.

title: Security Services Agent
description:
Career Opportunity

The Calgary TELUS Convention Centre (CTCC) hosts conventions, tradeshows, and meetings for national, international, and local groups. We are currently looking to hire full-time Security Services Agents in our Security Services Department.

The mandate of Security Services is to deliver professional and results-oriented security services to the CTCC business units, visitors, and clients, including, but not limited to, life safety and emergency response.

Reporting to the Manager, Security Services and Team Lead, the Security Services Agent is responsible for maintaining the security and safety of people and property within and surrounding the CTCC, +15 connections, and for providing ancillary business and customer services to other staff members, clients, and the public.

Due to the dynamic nature of this position, a high level of critical-thinking skills is required to meet the standards of this position and adequately perform situational risk and event-related assessments, interact with a variety of clientele, and implement sound judgment in situations requiring the use of discretion.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Under guidance and direction from the Manager, Security Services and Team Lead, Security Services, perform security operations for the CTCC while functioning ethically, efficiently, effectively, and with the utmost professionalism.
  • Monitor, investigate, patrol, and protect persons and/or property to deter or detect loss for persons, property, or premises under the care and control of the CTCC.
  • Perform investigations pertaining to, but not limited to, loss of or damage to property, premises, and/or persons under the care and control of the CTCC.
  • While operating within the legal authority and the policies/procedures of the CTCC, conduct searches of the person(s), personal property, or premises for the purpose of protection or loss prevention.
  • While operating within the legal authority and the policies/procedures of the CTCC, utilize authorized methods of physical subject control, arrest, and defensive tactics to remove or restrain individuals demonstrating criminal conduct or active damage to property, premises, and/or persons under the care and control of the CTCC.
  • Comply with legislation governing security and investigative services as defined in the Security Services and Investigators Act, the Security Services and Investigators Regulations, and the Security Services and Investigators Act Ministerial Regulations, including but not limited to maintaining license status, training qualifications, authorized equipment, reporting requirements, complaint processes and Code of Conduct.
  • Demonstrate an understanding of customer requirements and provide outstanding quality of service in accordance with company and industry standards.
  • Complete assigned duties in accordance with internal policies and procedures.
  • Facilitate response to emergency operations and incident response, including assuming the role of Incident Commander in a traditional Incident Command System setting.
  • Establish and maintain relations with external agencies, including neighbouring properties, local law enforcement, and municipal agencies.
  • Maintain access control by managing access control systems, including but not limited to creating, issuing, and tracking instruments of access control (cards, locks, keys).
  • Coordinate and complete event-related security requests and work orders as required.
  • Facilitate and coordinate third-party contracted security services, medical services and pay duty officer requirements as required.
  • Monitor alarm systems, access control, and surveillance system.
  • Complete and maintain records, logs, reports, inventories, and other documentation in compliance with regulatory authorities and CTCC policies and procedures.
  • Acquire and maintain adequate certification or training as required.
  • Adhere to CTCC and Occupational Health & Safety regulations and performance standards.
  • Liaise with clients, contractors, service providers, employees, and other stakeholders.
  • Undertake other duties and projects as required.

Requirements

To be considered for the listed position of Security Services Agent, all applicants must:

  • Be legally eligible to work in Canada
  • Be flexible to work a rotational shift under an Averaging Arrangement - including nights, weekends, and holidays as required.
  • Possess a High School Diploma or equivalent.
  • Possess and maintain a valid Government of Alberta Security Services license with no restrictions defined by the Security Services and Investigators Act & Regulations.
  • Possess a minimum of two (2) years of experience in a security and incident-response-related field.
  • Possess and maintain training requirements including, but not limited to, the following:
    • First Aid (Standard Level C with AED or equivalent).
    • Alberta Basic Security Training or equivalent.
  • Maintain a strong sense of personal integrity, confidentiality, and a consistent work ethic.
  • Work well under pressure with the ability to multi-task and manage time effectively.
  • Possess average technological skills and knowledge including, but not limited to, the following:
    • Windows 10 OS
    • Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook)
  • Display an exceptional level of excellence, professionalism, and pride in customer service.
  • Maintain strong interpersonal, conflict resolution, and verbal/written communication skills
  • Possess an aptitude for critical thinking, resourcefulness, and troubleshooting.
  • Be able to work in a team environment and/or independently as required.

Assets

  • Post-secondary (degree, diploma, or certificate) in a related field.
  • Solicitor General certified use-of-force training (HFRG or equivalent);
  • Incident Command System (ICS) training (100 or 200)
  • Verbal de-escalation and/or tactical communications training.
  • Working knowledge of OH&S regulations and risk assessment analysis.
  • Experience in a hospitality and/or high-level customer service environment.
  • Previous experience or knowledge of access control, CCTV, and report writing systems.
  • Previous experience with building life safety systems.

Physical Requirements

  • Standing on feet for long periods of time.
  • Physically fit to have the ability to lift heavy weight, walk in excess of 10 KM per shift, execute subject control, and execute defensive tactics.
  • Comfortable working at heights.
  • To be able to monitor video monitors and perform computer-related tasks.
  • To be able to discern colours.

Core Company Success Traits

The Calgary TELUS Convention Centre:

  • Is Calgary’s meeting place, bringing the community together in a central hub to connect, learn, innovate, celebrate, support and grow.
  • Connects Calgary with the global community, leveraging our assets to create opportunities that impact the lives of Calgarians and Canadians.
  • Takes pride in our city and in delivering Calgary’s message of hospitality, prosperity and enlightened growth to countless visitors.
  • Is honoured to promote Calgary to the world and to host hundreds of events each year.
  • Is responsible for promoting Calgary by working with partners to build Calgary’s reputation as the destination of choice.
  • Is committed to providing a productive, comfortable, sustainable environment to our guests and employees.

The Convention Centre offers a comprehensive salary and benefits program that includes life and dependent life insurance, short and long-term disability, health, and dental benefits, travel medical emergency insurance, flexible spending account, employee assistance program, pension plan, flex and bonus hours, wellness programs, educational opportunities, and access to a fitness center.

Individuals interested in applying for this position can submit a resume and cover letter to careers@calgary-convention.com . This posting will remain open until the position(s) has been filled. We thank all applicants for their interest.

title: Microsoft 365 Administrator
description:
WorkNomads is on the hunt for a Microsoft 365 Administrator to join our team!

Who We Are:

Microsoft 365 administration and support

    • Administer and troubleshoot Microsoft 365 services, primarily Entra ID, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams, and Intune.

    • Maintain users, groups, licenses, shared mailboxes, permissions, and collaboration resources.
    • Support mailbox administration, distribution lists, mail flow, and email security configurations.
    • Maintain SharePoint sites, access permissions, sharing settings, and lifecycle governance.

Identity, endpoints, and security

Automation and continuous improvement

    • Use PowerShell to simplify repetitive administration tasks and improve operational consistency.
    • Contribute to automation of user lifecycle, group management, license allocation, and access requests.
    • Support approved Power Automate and Microsoft Graph integrations where appropriate.
    • Identify outdated configurations, unused resources, unnecessary licenses, and opportunities to reduce manual effort.
    • Document improvements and ensure that automation includes appropriate approvals, error handling, and recovery procedures.

Digital workplace projects

    • Contribute to SharePoint cleanup, migration, restructuring, and improved information governance.
    • Support Microsoft 365 identity and access cleanup, including groups, shared mailboxes, naming conventions, and obsolete resources.
    • Participate in technical implementation projects, service transitions, and integrations.
    • Support the responsible adoption of Microsoft 365 Copilot and new workplace capabilities.

ICT Core operations and collaboration

    • Participate in shared ICT Core support activities, including device provisioning, onboarding, offboarding, and asset administration.
    • Troubleshoot endpoint and connectivity issues affecting digital workplace services.
    • Work with infrastructure colleagues and external vendors to resolve issues outside your primary specialization.
    • Collaborate with the Service Delivery Manager and other technical teams to implement service improvements.
    • Maintain clear technical documentation, knowledge-base articles, and operational runbooks.
    • Share knowledge with colleagues and provide practical guidance to end users.

Requirements

We want to hear from you if you have:

    • At least 3 years of hands-on experience administering Microsoft 365 in a production environment.
    • Strong practical knowledge of Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange Online, and Microsoft 365 administration.
    • Experience supporting SharePoint migration or Microsoft 365 tenant projects.
    • Working experience with SharePoint Online, Teams, and Intune, including troubleshooting and configuration.
    • Experience with user lifecycle management, permissions, MFA, groups, and license administration.
    • Practical PowerShell scripting experience for Microsoft 365 administration.
    • Experience managing or supporting Windows endpoints and device policies.
    • Good understanding of networking fundamentals, DNS, TCP/IP, and connectivity troubleshooting.
    • Experience using IT ticketing systems and working with incident, request, and change processes.
    • Ability to troubleshoot independently, identify root causes, and communicate solutions clearly.
    • Strong written and spoken English.
    • An organized, ownership-driven approach and willingness to document technical work.
    • A passion for continuous learning & collaboration in a global setting
    • A team player mentality and believe no one should be left behind regardless of background
  • Nice to have:
    • Experience with Microsoft Graph, Power Automate, or Power Platform.
    • Knowledge of Microsoft Defender, Purview, DLP, or Microsoft 365 Copilot administration.
    • Experience with Autopilot and macOS or mobile device management.
    • Familiarity with Microsoft 365 email authentication, including SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.
    • Relevant Microsoft certifications such as MS-102, MD-102, SC-300, or MS-700.
    • Familiarity with ITIL practices, Zero Trust, or ISO 27001-aligned environments.
    • Experience in remote-first, international, or growing organizations.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. ABOUT THE JOB

The Senior Supplier Industrialization Engineer, Electrical is a high-profile, cross functional position that plays an integral role in enabling development and production flow of Anduril’s critical supply base. You will work in close coordination with internal engineering, quality, supply chain and manufacturing departments as well as directly with suppliers to execute effective, creative and smart supply chain strategies to achieve production goals.

We're looking for a talented Senior Supplier Industrialization Engineer to expedite the qualification and implementation of product designs with our suppliers, optimizing these designs for quality, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness from early development through the entire product lifecycle.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own and manage the electrical commodities/subcategories (cables, harness, capacitors, connectors, PCB/PCBA, chips, etc.) to execute supplier production (NPI to full production) strategies across Anduril’s business lines
  • Be a force multiplier for the Supply Chain team and overall commodity strategy, demonstrating a strong sense of ownership, proactivity, technical excellence, creativity, self-direction, and courage
  • Vet Suppliers' production capabilities, factory lay out, facilities, workforce for supplier inclusion in Approved Supplier List
  • Support Supply Chain Product Sourcing Engineers (PSE), Supply Chain Global Strategic Sourcing Management (GSS) and Supplier Quality Engineers (SQE) in ensuring Suppliers' understanding and adherence to the criteria for part quality set by SQE
  • Own bringing up new production tooling & lines, development at Supplier as needed, at Supplier sites to ensure materials, processes & tools are capable of meeting product performance, quality (criteria set by SQE) and demand requirements
  • Own capacity expansion readiness and production ramp-up at Supplier
  • Establish and drive process performance and controls (SPC) reviews at Supplier
  • Identify and drive product and process improvements, factory layout optimization at Supplier sites to lower part cost, reduce supply risk, eliminate potential defects, and improve cycle time ​over the product lifecycle
  • Support SQE with root cause task force at Anduril by working in tandem with the Supply Chain team, Suppliers​, and be responsible for closing the loop of root cause corrective/preventative actions at Supplier

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, engineering, or related technical field
  • 6+ years of experience in supplier quality and industrialization within a manufacturing environment
  • Experience with specific category technical expertise, as applicable, electronics manufacturing, SMT processing, GD&T
  • Ability to travel at least 50% of the time
  • Ability to relocate, if not already local to be onsite in Costa Mesa, CA

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, or related technical field
  • Previous experience in defense, aerospace, automotive, high tech, or another related industry
  • Strong understanding of quality systems, standards, and certifications
  • Familiarity with developing high-tech products in a high-mix, low-volume environment
  • Exposure to working in a fast-pace, start-up environment
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. TS clearance
US Salary Range
$161,000—$212,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

  • No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

  • Please always verify communications:
    • Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
    • Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

  • Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

  • What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit .

title: Facilitator, Leadership ELA Math UnboundEd Planning Pathways (UPP) (CA, Midwest)
description:
About UnboundEd

We are a team of former classroom teachers, district and school leaders, curriculum writers, and education experts unified by our desire to see every student thrive in school.

Our commitment to every learner unites us. UnboundEd works side-by-side with teachers, coaches, principals, and district leaders to ensure every student has access to grade-level, engaging, affirming, and meaningful — GLEAM™ — instruction. By cultivating the mindsets, knowledge, and skills at the heart of truly transformative teaching and learning, we can break the predictability of historic achievement patterns so all kids thrive.

In 2023, UnboundEd joined forces with Pivot Learning and CORE Learning to expand our offerings and drive long-needed changes in instruction, especially in the highest-need schools.

Position Overview

We are seeking expert contract Facilitators across our Leadership, ELA, Math, and UnboundEd Planning Process (UPP) pathways to lead Local Learning Experiences in California and the Midwest United States.

Facilitators guide educators and school leaders through interactive, standards-aligned professional development focused on actionable instructional practices that expand access and opportunity for all learners. In this role, you will deliver UnboundEd-designed learning experiences, foster collaborative professional dialogue, and adapt your facilitation to meet the needs of participating educators while keeping learning grounded in high-quality instruction.

This is a contract position. Facilitators are engaged on an event-by-event basis.

Key Responsibilities

Workshop Facilitation & Content Delivery

  • Facilitate engaging, high-impact sessions for educators and school leaders across Leadership, ELA, Math, or UPP pathways during Local Learning Experiences.
  • Deliver UnboundEd-designed content with fidelity, adding your own expertise and examples to deepen, not replace, the core learning.
  • Present research-informed, standards-based content clearly, connecting session concepts to participants' real-world classroom and leadership practices.
  • Help educators reflect on and translate workshop learning into concrete action plans for their schools and districts, using varied checks for understanding to ensure learning lands.

Adult Learning & Group Dynamics

  • Create an inclusive, welcoming, and productive learning environment where adult learners feel comfortable taking risks and engaging in thoughtful dialogue.
  • Guide meaningful, participant-centered discussions around effective instruction, student impact, and addressing barriers to student success.

title: Senior Associate, Cyber Operations – Incident Response
description:
Job Description

The Senior Associate, Cyber Operations will join the Cyber Operations / Incident Response team and will be responsible for investigating, managing, and documenting cybersecurity incidents within a 24x7 security operations environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Monitor, investigate, and respond to cybersecurity alerts and incidents, identifying potential threats and assessing their impact on the organization.
  • Manage security incidents throughout the Incident Response lifecycle, including identification, containment, eradication, recovery, and lessons learned.
  • Investigate security events using Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR) technologies such as CrowdStrike, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE), Zscaler, or equivalent platforms.
  • Support threat identification, incident investigation, containment, and remediation activities.
  • Document incident findings, investigation details, actions taken, and resolution outcomes.
  • Use ServiceNow or similar platforms for incident ticketing, tracking, and case management.
  • Support investigations related to email security threats such as phishing and malicious emails using tools such as Proofpoint or equivalent technologies.
  • Leverage Threat Intelligence platforms, such as Recorded Future or equivalent solutions, to identify Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) and support incident investigations.
  • Work within a predominantly Microsoft Azure environment and support security monitoring and incident response activities across cloud-based systems.
  • Use scripting, preferably Python or Shell Script, to automate small repetitive security tasks when applicable.
  • Support security automation and orchestration activities using Cortex XSOAR or equivalent SOAR platforms when required.
  • Stay current with cybersecurity threats, technologies, and security practices and contribute to continuous improvement of incident response processes and controls.

Job Requirements

Must-have

  • 3–5 years of hands-on experience in Cybersecurity Incident Response / Incident Management.
  • Experience investigating and responding to cybersecurity alerts and incidents.
  • Hands-on experience with EDR technologies, such as CrowdStrike, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE), Zscaler, or equivalent platforms.
  • Solid understanding of the Incident Response lifecycle: Preparation, Identification, Containment, Eradication, Recovery, and Lessons Learned.
  • Ability to document incidents, investigations, actions taken, findings, and outcomes.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.
  • Availability to work rotating schedules according to operational needs, with schedule changes approximately every quarter.
  • Availability to work 100% remotely.

Preferred / Nice to Have

  • Experience with ServiceNow for security incident ticketing and case management.
  • Experience working in Microsoft Azure environments; approximately 80–90% of the current environment is Azure-based.
  • Basic scripting experience, preferably Python; Shell Script is also valuable.
  • Experience with Proofpoint or equivalent email security platforms.
  • Experience with Recorded Future or other Threat Intelligence platforms, including working with Indicators of Compromise (IOCs).
  • Experience with Cortex XSOAR or another SOAR platform for security automation and orchestration.
  • Exposure to Threat Hunting and Digital Forensics.

Preferred Certifications

Certifications are desirable but not mandatory. Particularly valued certifications include:

  • GCIH – GIAC Certified Incident Handler
  • GCFE – GIAC Certified Forensic Examiner
  • GCFA – GIAC Certified Forensic Analyst
  • Microsoft Azure certifications, such as AZ-900 – Microsoft Azure Fundamentals

Other relevant cybersecurity certifications may also be considered.

title: Credit Operations Intern
description:
POSITION: Credit Operations Intern (Full Time)

LOCATION: Bogotá, Colombia

REPORTING TO: Director of Credit


BACKGROUND

Global Partnerships (GP) is an impact-first fund manager dedicated to expanding opportunity for people living in poverty. Impact-first investing means investing in a way that seeks the greatest possible social impact, while seeking to preserve capital with a modest financial return for investors. GP believes that impact-first investing has an essential role to play in advancing sustainable solutions to poverty for millions of people worldwide.


GP creates and manages impact-first investment funds that make loans and early-stage investments in social enterprises serving people living in poverty, primarily in Latin America and Africa. The GP team is comprised of mission-driven, dedicated, high-performing colleagues working primarily from offices in Seattle, Washington (USA), Bogotá, Colombia, and Nairobi, Kenya. To learn more about Global Partnerships, please visit our website at .


ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The Credit Operations Intern supports GP’s Social Investment Team (SIT) by executing established portfolio monitoring processes, maintaining high-quality data, producing routine reports, and making incremental improvements to existing tools and workflows. This is a hands-on role focused on accuracy, timeliness, and clear communication across teams. As an intern, you will be exposed to GP’s full investment cycle, learning about the impact investing space while sharpening your skills.

  • Location: Bogotá regional office (hybrid)
  • Reporting to: Investment Analysis Officer
  • Type: 12-month Internship (full-time)
  • Compensation: $2.5 million COP per month plus benefits


Core Responsibilities:

  • Drive and promote a strong data-informed culture throughout GP and manage high-quality and flexible credit and investment data systems.
  • Execute established portfolio data workflows: collect, validate, and upload partner financial/operational data on schedule.
  • Maintain data integrity: monitor completeness, resolve discrepancies, and document fixes.
  • Support the implementation of AI tools to make data collection and verification processes more efficient and effective.
  • Produce recurring reports (internal/external) using existing templates and dashboards.

title: Sr. Database Administrator
description:
Position Overview

The Senior Database Administrator is a highly skilled technical role responsible for the performance, availability, security and reliability of enterprise database systems supporting critical business operations. This role includes Microsoft SQL Server database administration, performance monitoring and tuning, migrations, lifecycle management, high availability, disaster recovery and advanced troubleshooting. The Senior DBA will provide technical leadership, act as the final escalation point for complex database issues and collaborate across teams to architect and deliver scalable, secure and reliable database solutions.

Key Responsibilities:


  • Provide technical leadership on database systems and solutions and act as the final technical escalation point for all database-related issues.
  • Manage, maintain, implement and support Microsoft SQL Server databases in a high-availability environment hosted in the cloud (SQL on VMs), using Always-On Availability Groups, mirroring and replication.
  • Plan and execute SQL Server upgrades, migrations and lifecycle management initiatives.
  • Perform database capacity planning, storage forecasting and resource utilization analysis.
  • Conduct research, analysis, monitoring and profiling to improve database performance, functionality, recoverability and availability.
  • Ensure data integrity, quality and security across all database systems.
  • Participate in the Disaster Recovery Planning and Testing to manage and validate backup, restore and recovery strategies and perform regular recovery testing to ensure recoverability of business-critical databases.
  • Architect and maintain databases for optimal performance and scalability.
  • Manage database maintenance activities including index optimization, statistics maintenance and SQL Agent job management.
  • Deploy and maintain database security controls and support security initiatives and audits.
  • Cross-train peers and team members and provide guidance on complex database issues.
  • Set and maintain high standards and best practices for database systems while refining, automating and documenting DBA processes through diagrams, SOPs and scripts.
  • Manage and tune database monitoring systems.
  • Participate in on-call rotation supporting business-critical systems.
  • Participate in development code reviews to educate on SQL coding standards and best practices.
  • Collaborate with developers, BI, management and other IT staff to ensure database system reliability, performance and provide solutions to complex data challenges.
  • Evaluate, test, and recommend new technologies and tools.

Basic Qualifications:


  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • Fully Bilingual in English and Spanish
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience administering enterprise production database environments.
  • Excellent analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience supporting mission-critical production environments.
  • Expertise in Microsoft SQL Server including Always On, replication, mirroring and performance tuning.
  • Advanced troubleshooting and performance tuning experience including execution plans, indexing strategies, wait statistics and query optimization.
  • Familiarity with Azure cloud services and experience managing databases in virtual machines within Azure.
  • Knowledge of database monitoring tools.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to mentor other team members.
  • Familiarity with database security best practices, high availability and disaster recovery.
  • Understanding of ETL vs ELT concepts.
  • Understanding of OLTP vs OLAP, BI tools and their integration with databases.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in relational database administration including MS SQL Server, Azure SQL Managed Instance, Azure SQL Database.
  • Experience with PowerShell or other scripting languages.
  • Experience with database migration to Azure SQL.
  • Experience in architecting databases for near real-time reporting.
  • Experience with database automation, CI/CD pipelines and DevOps practices.
  • Experience using source control systems such as Git.
  • Experience with enterprise database monitoring platforms such as Redgate, Dynatrace, SolarWinds.
  • Experience deploying and maintaining NoSQL database technologies such as CosmosDB.
  • Relevant Certifications.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities

  • Evaluate material availability for upcoming aircraft, work orders and assembly activities across defined readiness horizons.
  • Identify missing, blocked, incorrect or unavailable parts and maintain one accurate, prioritized shortage and material-readiness overview.
  • Coordinate shortage actions with Tactical Purchasing, Logistics, Quality, Engineering, Production Planning and Production, including clear owners and required dates.
  • Lead material-readiness and missing-parts meetings, follow up open actions and escalate risks that could affect the assembly schedule.
  • Verify that required material has been received, inspected, released, picked and made available at the correct point of use before work begins.
  • Monitor parts affected by quality issues, engineering or configuration changes, repairs, substitutions and inventory discrepancies until final resolution.
  • Support recovery plans by evaluating material constraints and communicating feasible material-availability dates to Production and Production Planning.
  • Act as the primary material-status contact for Production and provide timely, accurate answers regarding shortages, priorities and expected availability.
  • Develop and maintain KPIs and reports covering work-order readiness, shortages by aircraft, shortage aging, blocked material and action closure.

Other Duties/Responsibilities

  • Maintain material-status information, shortage records and relevant SAP transactions accurately and in a timely manner.
  • Support continuous-improvement activities related to material readiness, shortage management, information flow and production support.
  • Work with a high level of ownership, urgency and flexibility, particularly during assembly-line startup and ramp-up.
  • Perform other duties and support cross-functional projects as assigned.

title: Digital Verification Engineer
location: San Francisco, Bay Area OR Pittsburgh, PA OR Austin, TX
description:
Efficient Computer is rethinking computing from the ground up to solve one of AI's biggest challenges: energy. Our Fabric architecture delivers a 10–100x improvement in energy efficiency for general-purpose computation, including AI, while supporting familiar programming languages and software frameworks—unlocking new possibilities for autonomous machines, intelligent infrastructure, wearables, and space systems. With our first processor, Electron E1, now shipping in volume and more than $97 million in Series B financing recently announced, we're accelerating customer deployments and scaling our architecture to data center performance. Join us to build the hardware and software that bring intelligence wherever it's needed and help shape the next generation of computing.

We are looking for a Design Verification Engineer to join our newly formed verification team and own the functional verification of blocks and subsystems in our SoC, including Efficient's proprietary Fabric technology. You'll work alongside senior DV engineers, RTL designers, and architects to build testbenches, close coverage, and find bugs before silicon does. This is a great opportunity to grow your skills while having a real influence on our products and processes as we move from initial product development to market release and scaled volume production.

What You'll Do

  • Develop and maintain UVM/SystemVerilog testbenches, sequences, and tests for block- and subsystem-level verification.
  • Write verification plans from design specifications in collaboration with design and architecture teams.
  • Write SystemVerilog assertions and functional coverage models, and drive coverage to closure.
  • Debug simulation failures, working with designers to root-cause and fix issues.
  • Contribute to regression infrastructure, automation, and dashboards that track verification progress.
  • Support gate-level simulation and other sign-off activities.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Education: Bachelor's or Master's/PhD degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
  • Experience: 4+ years of experience in ASIC/SoC design verification, with multiple projects taken through tapeout.
  • UVM and SystemVerilog: Hands-on experience building and extending UVM testbench components (agents, scoreboards, sequences) and constrained-random tests.
  • Coverage: Experience defining functional coverage and driving code and functional coverage closure at block or subsystem level.
  • Assertions: Working knowledge of SystemVerilog Assertions.
  • Debug Skills: Ability to independently debug simulation failures using waveforms, logs, and design knowledge.
  • Scripting & Automation: Proficiency in Python for test automation, log analysis, and regression flows.
  • Communication: Ability to clearly report verification status and issues to the team.

Ways to Stand Out

  • C/C++ experience for reference models or DPI-based verification.
  • Exposure to formal verification (JasperGold or similar).
  • Experience building or using AI agentic flows for DV.
  • Knowledge of computer architecture or dataflow architectures.
  • Exposure to power-aware verification (UPF)

We offer a competitive base salary for this role, generally ranging from $130,000 to $180,000, plus a 10% annual bonus, meaningful equity, and comprehensive benefits. Final compensation will depend on experience, level, and location, with flexibility for the right candidate.

Why Join Efficient?

Build what's next. At Efficient, you'll tackle big challenges with room to take ownership and make an impact. We back you with competitive pay, equity, a 401(k) match, company-paid benefits, paid parental leave, and flexibility—plus opportunities to grow your skills and career as we scale.

title: Halassistent søges til Snedsted Hallen
description:
Vil du kombinere praktisk drift med ansvar – og blive en vigtig del af et idrætscenter i udvikling?

Snedsted Hallen er en arbejdsplads, hvor dagene sjældent er ens, og hvor vi hver dag gør os umage for at give vores gæster en god oplevelse – og samtidig har vi stor fleksibilitet.

I Snedsted Hallen søger vi en halassistent, som har lyst til at blive en vigtig del af hverdagen i faciliteter, der hver dag danner ramme om idræt, fællesskab og massevis af møder mellem mennesker.

Hos os følger arbejdstiden aktivitetsniveauet. Derfor arbejder vi efter årsnorm. Det betyder typisk at vinterhalvåret byder på mange aktiviteter og arrangementer, mens der i sommerperioden typisk er mulighed for mere frihed og afspadsering.

Vi søger en kollega, der trives med en aktiv arbejdsdag, tager ansvar og har lyst til både at være en del af den daglige drift og fungere som sparring om hallens fortsatte udvikling samt blive en vigtig del af det positive arbejdsfællesskab, som kendetegner Snedsted Hallen.

Dine opgaver

Størstedelen af din arbejdstid foregår ude i faciliteterne, hvor du sammen med dine kolleger sikrer, at brugerne møder indbydende og velfungerende rammer.
En betydelig del af arbejdet vil også foregå i svømmehallen som livredder og eventuel underviser.

Dine opgaver vil blandt andet være

  • Praktiske drifts- og vedligeholdelsesopgaver

  • Livredning (Uddannelsen kan tages efter ansættelse) samt. evt. svømmeundervisning

  • Klargøring og rengøring af faciliteter

  • Kundeservice: Telefon, motionscenter, café mv.

  • Opstilling og nedtagning til aktiviteter, kampe og arrangementer

  • Service og kontakt til brugere, foreninger og samarbejdspartnere

  • Praktiske opgaver i forbindelse med arrangementer, kurser og events.

Som halassistent kan du samtidig få en vigtig rolle som centerlederens stedfortræder. Når centerlederen ikke er til stede, kan du hjælpe du med at koordinere dagens opgaver, prioritere arbejdsindsatsen og sikre, at den daglige drift fungerer.

Vi forestiller os, at du

  • Trives med en aktiv arbejdsdag og ikke er bange for at tage fat

  • Tager ansvar, er mødestabil og følger opgaverne til dørs

  • Kan bevare overblikket, når der sker mange ting på én gang

  • Har hænderne godt skruet på, og eventuelt har en håndværkeruddannelse

  • Er en holdspiller, der bidrager positivt til fællesskabet og hjælper til, hvor der er brug for det

  • Er serviceminded og gerne går den ekstra meter for at skabe gode oplevelser for vores gæster

  • Har grundlæggende IT-kompetencer

    Det vigtigste er, at du har lyst til at tage ansvar, tage fat, bidrage til fællesskabet og hjælpe med at få hverdagen til at fungere.

    Vi tilbyder

  • En alsidig stilling med stor variation i arbejdsopgaverne

  • Mulighed for at kombinere praktisk arbejde med sparring og udvikling

  • Et godt kollegialt fællesskab med humor og en uformel omgangstone

  • En arbejdsplads med mange forskellige brugere, aktiviteter og oplevelser

  • En hverdag med mange små møder med og smil fra centrets brugere

Arbejdstid

Stillingen er på gennemsnitligt 25 - 35 timer om ugen og følger en årsnorm. Ved ansøgning skriv gerne hvilket timetal, du vil foretrække.

Du indgår i et vagtrul med arbejde hver 3. weekend samt en fast hverdagsaften. I perioder med mange aktiviteter og arrangementer kan der forekomme ekstra vagter, som planlægges i tæt dialog med resten af teamet.

Praktiske oplysninger

Arbejdsstedet er Snedsted Hallen, Øster Alle 10, 7752 Snedsted
Start dato: 1. januar 2027 eller snarest muligt derefter.

Ansættelsesvilkår

Stillingen er med en årsnorm svarende til 25 - 35 timer ugentligt.

Løn og ansættelsesvilkår fastsættes individuelt på baggrund af kvalifikationer, erfaring og stillingens indhold.

Spørgsmål?

Har du spørgsmål til stillingen er du velkommen til at kontakte centerleder Kristian Pilgaard på 24404581

Ansøgning

Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig og måske byde dig velkommen i teamet hos Snedsted Hallen.

Send din ansøgning og CV til kristian@snedstedhallen.dk senest søndag den 15. november.

Ved ansættelse indhentes der børneattest.

title: Technical Project Manager
description:
Job Title: Technical Project Manager

Location: Milpitas, CA

Department: Standards

Salary Range: $118,200- $147,000 per year


This position is open to candidates residing in U.S. states where the organization is currently authorized to employ individuals. Eligible work locations will be confirmed during the hiring process. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and maintain ongoing work authorization throughout employment without the need for current or future employer sponsorship.


INTRODUCTION OF SEMI

Although we’re small, we’re mighty and influence and impact society at large positively. At SEMI, we offer opportunities to connect and interact with world leaders, industry legends, and rising stars. We help our members develop public and private policies to strengthen global supply chains and promote business growth and prosperity. Learn and grow professionally through career opportunities such as rotational assignments. Contribute by influencing and impacting an industry that is the foundation for innovation and positive change in areas like environmental sustainability, thought leadership, and workforce development. We take pride in offering work-life balance so you can live your personal and professional life to the fullest.

As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome all to apply

THE ROLE:

The Technical Project Manager position is responsible for managing technical and supply-chain projects that are ultimately developed into global industry standards. Standards are voluntary technical agreements between suppliers and customers, aimed at improving product quality and reliability at a reasonable price and steady supply. Standards ensure compatibility and inter-operability of goods and services.


The position has the responsibility for facilitating various SEMI technology industry groups in identifying critical standardization areas, architecting the standardization framework, and then driving these initiatives successfully through a consensus-based process. This role will work in collaboration with global, cross-functional team members to drive these SEMI technology initiatives, grow membership base and deepen SEMI Standards presence in the microelectronics and adjacent industries.


This is a highly visible, customer-facing position that requires strong communication and presentation skills. The role must provide public presentations, information, and articles pertaining to SEMI Standards and other SEMI technology initiatives. The position must ensure that programs and initiatives meet SEMI’s charter and can be provided within the existing budget. Responsibilities also include collaboration with SEMI internal marketing in determining the right methods and activities for marketing of SEMI Standards initiatives.


This is a full-time, exempt position and reports to the Director of Standards at SEMI Milpitas Office.


CORE RESPONSIBILITIES:

Drive technical and supply chain projects for development into SEMI Standards

· Coordinate and manage standards development projects originating from SEMI industry groups, technology communities, and related initiatives.

· Support SEMI Technology Coalitions in developing industry frameworks and best practices that can be translated into SEMI Standards requirements, guidelines, and related deliverables.

· Plan, coordinate, and facilitate meetings, workshops, and working sessions to drive consensus and advance technical objectives.

· Capture key decisions and outcomes, track action items, and coordinate follow-up activities.

· Recruit and engage project champions, contributors, and subject matter experts to build broad industry participation and support project objectives.

· Work with a matrixed team of industry volunteers and staff to ensure projects and deliverables are completed on time and on budget.

· Foster alignment and collaboration with industry associations, standards organizations, and other stakeholders whose activities support shared objectives.


Raise visibility of SEMI Standards Initiatives and Grow SEMI Standards branding

· Promote and raise industry awareness of SEMI Standards initiatives through technical workshops, white papers, web articles, newsletters, speaking engagements, webinars, social media, and other SEMI marketing channels.


Build and strengthen connections with critical stakeholders

· Provide regular updates of ongoing projects to various SEMI business units including regional offices

· Present on status and updates to related SEMI Standards Program committees and task forces


Champion SEMI Standards Development

· Provide technical writing support in drafting standards documentation

· Facilitate the transition of completed projects to formal SEMI Standards development

· Assist in appointing leadership

· Provide guidance on the Standards development process

· Assist activity initialization steps such as task force formation and new activity statement of work (SOW)

· Promote Usage of SEMI Standards

· With subject matter experts, develop Standards training and e-learning courses

· Support conformity assessment efforts related to SEMI Standards by engaging SEMI Technology Coalitions and industry expert networks.

· Assist in the Standards publication process to speed up time to market


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

· SEMI being sought to drive standards engineering projects, not only in the current industries it serves but also in emerging technology & application spaces.

· More companies join SEMI (and existing members renew their membership) to engage in these Standards initiatives.

· SEMI grows its Standards portfolio, providing the industries we serve valuable, high-impact standards leading to increased sales and revenue.

· SEMI Standards brand is recognized in non-established markets as well as in future SEMI growth areas.


CRITICAL SKILLS:

· Engineering mindset with the ability to drive technical projects from concept through execution.

· Strong organizational savvy; able to build relationships, influence stakeholders, and create alignment across functions.

· Collaborative, team-oriented approach with the ability to work effectively across diverse cultures and with business, technology, government, and academic stakeholders.

· Self-directed, proactive, and adaptable; able to take direction and execute independently.

· Strong verbal, written, presentation, and documentation skills.

· Effective project and time management skills, including the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

· Strong meeting facilitation and cross-functional collaboration skills.

· Event coordination and social media marketing capabilities.

· Persistent, focused, and low-ego approach to achieving results.


KNOWLEDGE OR EXPERIENCE:

· B.S./B.A. in business or engineering

· Minimum 3 years of experience in the semiconductor industry and/or trade association industry is required

· 2-3 years of experience in program/project management, PMP certification preferred

· Demonstrated experience in working with culturally diverse staff and customers preferred – multilingual abilities in a language of SEMI presence (e.g., China, Korea, Taiwan) is a plus

· Hands-on experience in the development of standards (if from industry) or management of standards development (if from a trade association or professional association) is preferred

· Proficiency with Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel. Experience with project management software is a plus

· Expected travel < 10%


THE IDEAL CANDIDATE:

The ideal candidate will have program management experience with prior roles in the semiconductor industry and demonstrates working knowledge of semiconductor technology, industry players, challenges, and trends. You have an extreme customer focus mindset and has worked with international teams especially in a collaborative environment. The candidate is a process-oriented problem-solver who can manage multiple issues and projects with limited resources. You demonstrates strong inter-personal skills and embodies can-do, positive attitude.


About SEMI

SEMI® is the global industry association connecting over 4,000 companies and 1.5 million professionals worldwide across the semiconductor and electronics design and manufacturing supply chain. We accelerate member collaboration on solutions to top industry challenges through Advocacy, Workforce Development, Sustainability, Supply Chain Management and other programs. Our SEMICON® expositions and events, technology coalitions, standards and market intelligence help advance our members’ business growth and innovations in design, devices, equipment, materials, services and software, enabling smarter, faster, more secure electronics. Visit www.semi.org, contact a regional office, and connect with SEMI on LinkedIn and X to learn more.


ABOUT SEMI STANDARDS

The SEMI International Standards Program is a key service offered by SEMI for the benefit of the worldwide electronics design and manufacturing industries. Standards help the industry meet the challenges of increasing productivity, encouraging innovation, global expansion and training new workers. The program operates as a neutral forum for exchanging information between suppliers and users, which results in the production of timely and technically accurate specifications and guidelines. Companies utilizing standards can decrease manufacturing costs, increase reliability and productivity, and access global markets. Standards transcend international boundaries. More importantly, SEMI Standards development conducted on an international basis spurs the dialogue that results in joint ventures, technology licenses, and sales. Standards are not just developed by and for engineers; their use is also a management tool, often a business strategy, and consequently should be accompanied by high level support for standards-setting activities. The program, started over 50 years ago in North America, was expanded in 1985 to include programs in Europe and Japan, and now also has technical committees in China, Korea and Taiwan. Over 5,000 technologists worldwide, representing all levels of the supply chain, convene to resolve an increasing variety of process and product related issues.

title: Senior Inventory Analyst
description:

Essential Skills, Education and Experience:

• Relevant experience with databases and spreadsheets.

• Familiarity with supply chain and inventory control processes (i.e.: turnover, safety stock, reorder points, carrying costs, demand forecasting, etc.)

• Excellent communication and organizational skills.

• Strong analytical, time management, and problem-solving skills.

• Experience in data entry, analysis, and reporting.

• Working knowledge of MS Office, Excel, ERP Systems (ie: Epicor), MS Teams.

title: Director of Finance
description:
New Orleans, Louisiana
Full-Time | In-Person
Reports to the CEO and President
Base Salary: $150,000 annually


WHO WE ARE

French Truck Coffee is a growing, privately held specialty coffee company based in New Orleans. Our business includes 14 cafés, wholesale coffee, e-commerce, a coffee roastery, and a commissary supporting our retail locations.

We care deeply about coffee, hospitality, and the communities we serve. We have grown by staying close to our customers and operations, moving quickly when something needs attention, and expecting leaders to take real ownership of their work.

As the company has grown, our financial needs have become more complex. We are now ready to bring our accounting and financial reporting fully in-house and are looking for an experienced financial leader to help guide the company through its next stage.

WHAT THIS JOB REALLY IS

The Director of Finance will be French Truck Coffee’s senior financial leader, a member of the Executive Leadership Team, and the primary financial adviser to the CEO, President, and ownership.

This is more than a traditional Controller position. The Director of Finance will help shape company strategy, annual priorities, capital allocation, financing decisions, and plans for growth. This person will translate financial and operational information into clear recommendations that help ownership and department leaders make better decisions.

It is also a hands-on role. The Director of Finance will work closely with our Administrative Manager to transition accounting and financial reporting from outside providers to an internally managed function. That means taking direct responsibility for the monthly close, financial statements, reconciliations, cash-flow forecasting, and the systems and controls behind them.

This opportunity may be an especially strong next step for an experienced Controller, Assistant Controller, Finance Manager, or second-ranking finance leader who is ready to lead an entire finance function. It may also appeal to a current Director of Finance who wants direct access to ownership and greater influence over company strategy and operations.

We care more about the scope of your experience, your readiness to lead, and your willingness to remain involved in the details than whether you have previously held the title of Director of Finance or Chief Financial Officer.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Partner with Ownership and Company Leadership

• Serve as the primary financial adviser to the CEO, President, and ownership.

• Participate actively on the Executive Leadership Team and help shape long-term strategy, annual priorities, and plans for growth.

• Translate financial information into clear, practical recommendations for department leaders and other non-financial audiences.

Lead Financial Planning and Decision Support

• Develop annual budgets, rolling forecasts, cash-flow projections, executive dashboards, and key performance indicators.

• Analyze company, café, department, and business-channel performance to identify risks, opportunities, and potential improvements.

NOT A FIT IF…

GREAT FIT IF…

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Maritime Division has assembled a diverse team of experts in software, robotics, artificial intelligence, sensor fusion, and data analysis to create software and hardware solutions that radically evolve the capabilities of our customers. We are fielding the next generation of autonomous systems to tackle the extremely challenging industry demands of maritime operations. Anduril has brought to market a unique, ultra-long-range, full-ocean-depth underwater vessel platform and a completely refreshed maritime vehicle and flexible manufacturing architecture that scales from "small" to "extra-large" vehicle sizes. Today, Anduril is executing on billion-dollar contracts while simultaneously performing Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) AUV operations.

We are continuing to expand our product portfolio, now moving into the surface maritime domain. Products like Dive-XL, Dive-LD, Copperhead, Seabed Sentry, and surface products in the pipeline will create a system-of-systems that enable a multitude of autonomous missions across all maritime domains. If you are passionate about solving problems that have real impact and working on systems that directly contribute to achieving national strategic priorities, we want you to join Anduril's Maritime Division and help us build the future of defense capability.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Senior Systems Engineer to join the Maritime Enabling Technology (MET) team, based in Quincy, MA. MET serves the entire Maritime Division, developing shared technologies, common interfaces, and enabling capabilities across all product lines. In this role, you will be the primary MET Systems Engineering presence in Quincy, acting as the connective tissue between MET and co-located program teams across multiple business lines. The role blends systems engineering with technical program management: you will drive cross-system integration, manage stakeholder alignment and ensure that decisions on one product don't create downstream problems for another. This is a high-autonomy position that requires a proactive, independent operator with strong conviction and effective communication skills at every level.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Serve as the primary MET Systems Engineering point of contact in Quincy, engaging daily with co-located program teams across multiple Maritime business lines
  • Own cross-program systems integration and interface definition, ensuring that enabling technologies developed by MET are adopted smoothly across products
  • Drive stakeholder alignment across Designated Engineers, Chief Engineers, and program leads, translating program needs into MET development priorities and communicating MET capabilities and constraints back to programs
  • Identify and manage cross-system implications of technical decisions, ensuring that changes in one product area do not create integration risks or incompatibilities in others
  • Contribute to architecture, requirements definition, and verification strategy for shared subsystems, common interfaces (including Lattice integration), and enabling capabilities
  • Support the full product lifecycle - from design and rapid prototyping through integration, test, deployment, and sustainment of complex autonomous systems
  • Mentor engineers across teams, building systems engineering capacity and contributing to a culture of cross-functional collaboration within Maritime

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, related technical field or equivalent professional experience
  • 7–12 years of professional engineering experience, with demonstrated depth in systems engineering, systems integration, or a closely related technical discipline
  • Proven ability to work across organizational and technical boundaries - you have been the person who connects teams, resolves interface conflicts, and drives alignment
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with senior technical leadership, program managers, and working-level engineers
  • Experience acting as a technical lead, program integrator, or TPM for multi-disciplinary engineering teams
  • High ownership and a bias toward action - comfortable operating with autonomy in a geographically distributed team, with limited day-to-day oversight
  • Capacity to think holistically across complex systems - understanding how subsystem-level decisions propagate through an integrated product architecture
  • Experience with requirements definition, interface specification, system verification, and integration planning for hardware-software systems
  • Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with the design, integration, and operation of robotic and/or autonomous systems (maritime experience is a plus but not required)
  • Familiarity with defense acquisition, product delivery lifecycles, or working within a DoD customer environment
  • Experience with common middleware/integration frameworks for autonomous platforms
  • Background in one or more of: perception systems, navigation, autonomy software, sensor integration, communications systems, or power/energy systems for unmanned platforms
  • Experience within a rapid-iteration, hardware-software co-development environment

title: Manager, Data Quality and Performance
description:
Position Summary

The Manager, Data Quality and Performance provides leadership and oversight for compliance, quality assurance, performance monitoring, and driving continuous improvement across PhilaWorks contracted programs. This position supervises a team of analysts and specialists and is responsible for establishing effective monitoring practices, strengthening operational processes, coordinating internal and external audits, and ensuring resolution of identified issues.

This position serves as a strategic partner to internal departments and contracted providers, using data performance analysis to identify and mitigate risks, enhance data quality, support compliance with federal, state, and local requirements, and position the organization and its partners to successfully meet programmatic goals.


Essential Functions

  1. Oversee the development and implementation of internal monitoring and quality assurance frameworks for contracted programs, including desk audits, data validation, risk assessments, and root cause analyses to elevate performance standards among partner programs.
  2. Oversee the end-to-end process for external monitoring events, from pre-audit quality checks to the execution of state and federal validation cycles.
  3. Develop, implement, and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs), organizational workflows, tools, and other resources that support consistent and effective operations.
  4. Monitor compliance with applicable workforce development requirements, including WIOA, EARN, and other federal, state, and locally funded programs.
  5. Lead continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen operational processes, data collection, and reporting across funding streams to ensure alignment with programmatic goals.
  6. Analyze procedural problems and identify process waste to negotiate and implement necessary changes with stakeholders.
  7. Ensure data validation and external audit efforts for all programs (WIOA, EARN, etc.) are executed effectively and within strict deadlines.
  8. Mobilize staff for pre-audit activities and coordinate the implementation of standard work for audit readiness according to established SOPs.
  9. Direct post-audit analysis and manage the submission of official Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) and quarterly narratives to external agencies. Lead the development and submission of WIOA Negotiated Goals.
  10. Design and enforce comprehensive program monitoring and control plans to heighten quality standards and maintain acceptable data error margins.
  11. Partner with Research & Analysis and other internal teams to investigate data anomalies, identify root causes, and develop strategies to improve data quality and program performance.
  12. Evaluate Provider Performance across programmatic, fiscal, and compliance domains of service delivery to participants. Generate insights and reports on provider performance for leadership review.
  13. Oversee departmental staff by directing aspects of talent management, including workforce planning, recruitment and selection, onboarding, performance management, coaching, professional development, succession planning, employee engagement, retention, collaboration, accountability, communication, and a shared vision.
  14. Manage local Continuous Improvement Plan (CIP) processes, including formal review of submissions, structuring quarterly partner touchpoints, identifying improvement priorities, and monitoring progress for centers and providers.
  15. Build effective working relationships with internal departments, contracted providers, government agencies, and other external partners.
  16. Translate complex compliance, data, and process requirements into clear guidance and actionable recommendations for varied audiences.
  17. Represent the organization at external meetings, forums, and conferences, presenting content on workforce development, data compliance, and local performance.
  18. Perform other job-related duties as assigned.

description:

Each associate provides a service that directly or indirectly affects patients, families, other team members, and the public. We strive to excel in providing the highest quality healthcare and customer service possible, which is incumbent upon the excellence and commitment of our leaders and caregivers.

CMA's (Certified Medication Aide)

The Job

The CMA will support the community by ensuring residents are well cared for and receive accurate medications as ordered by the physician/physician extender in accordance with established nursing standards, standards of medication aide practices, state and federal requirements, and guidelines of the community related to medication administration.

Schedule:

  • 8 Hour Shifts
  • Day, Evening Shifts

Full-Time Benefits

  • Very Competitive Pay
  • Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) and Holidays
  • Medical
  • Dental
  • Vision
  • Company-paid life insurance & LTD/AD&D insurance
  • Short-Term Disability
  • Supplemental Insurances (Hospital Indemnity, Cancer Policies, Legal Plans, & More!)

Responsibilities

  • Obtain report from licensed nurse/CMA being relieved and record sufficient information related to medication administration to implement accurate changes to medication orders.
  • Administer medications to residents in an accurate, timely manner to include, but not limited to, correct resident/correct medication/correct dose/correct route/correct time.
  • Observe residents for effectiveness of drug therapy and occurrence of adverse effects. Report immediately to licensed nurse.
  • Document resident cares related to medication administration, related monitoring, and report to the licensed nurse any occurrence of observed adverse effects/change in resident's condition.
  • Notify licensed nurse of observed changes in residents’ conditions, medication errors, medication not available, and any other observations.
  • Perform duties of Certified Nurse Aide as assigned.
  • Follow comprehensive care plans related to medication administration based on each resident’s needs and his/her comprehensive assessment as assigned.
  • Participate in Community education programs.
  • Promptly report observed changes in residents’ conditions to the licensed nurse.
  • Respond to residents’ call for assistance promptly.
  • Verify accuracy of narcotic count; check emergency kit and exchange keys.
  • Obtain in-service hours required.
  • Observe infection control procedures.
  • Perform other related duties as directed by his/her supervisor.
  • Store medications accurately and appropriately, monitor drug expiration dates and follow process for destruction.

Qualifications

  • Enjoy working in a skilled nursing facility setting, eager to improve and continuously learn new skills
  • Ability to lift and/or move up to 50 pounds with physical capability to perform job-related duties
  • Validated ability to act in a compassionate and supportive manner
  • Prior experience in a healthcare environment (minimum of 1 year); preferably in long term care
  • Willingness to enforce health and safety standards
  • Supportive and compassionate
  • Take pride in providing high quality care

Must-Haves for Role

  • High School Diploma or equivalent
  • Certified Medication Aide in the State of Texas
  • CPR certification (preferred)
  • Reliable transportation
